name: Amami-Oshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, Northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island
description: This World Heritage site protects patches of subtropical rainforest on four islands in Japan's far southwest, strung along the Ryukyu chain between the East China Sea and the Pacific. The forests, about 42,700 hectares in all and uninhabited, shelter many species found nowhere else. Among them are the Amami rabbit and the Ryukyu long-haired rat, ancient lineages with no living relatives.
